hypotheses.claim_boundary: Supports a structured-retrieval advantage for this frozen portrayal task family, model, graph, corpus, and evaluator; not universal GraphRAG superiority or zero hallucination.
controls: matched Text-RAG and GraphRAG evidence-token ceiling
hypotheses.hypothesis_id: RQ1 comparison proposition (no frozen H1 identifier)
hypotheses.hypothesis_text: Explicit geographic knowledge grounding improves accurate and traceable answers to the frozen mapping questions under the LLM-only, Text-RAG, and GraphRAG comparison.
hypotheses.independent_variable: Retrieval architecture: no retrieval, ranked provenance-bearing text chunks, or typed graph retrieval and projection.
negative_evidence: GraphRAG and Text-RAG tied on geometry accuracy
GraphRAG recorded two parser-induced contradictions in one wording
GraphRAG exact 6/6 answers occurred in only 3 of 11 variants and incurred greater latency/token cost
unsupported historical claim and independent grounding/coverage failures are rejected by the deterministic validator
positive_evidence: GraphRAG mean requirement accuracy 75.76% versus Text-RAG 45.45% and LLM-only 15.15%
GraphRAG mean coverage 86.36% versus Text-RAG 68.18% and LLM-only 40.91%
GraphRAG recorded 96 supported and zero unsupported retrieval-grounded claims
hypotheses.residual_finding: The Text-RAG baseline uses deterministic feature hashing rather than a modern multilingual embedding, the evaluator vocabulary is bounded, and performance is wording-sensitive.
hypotheses.validator: Deterministic bounded claim-grounding and six-category coverage validator; zero validator model calls.

hypotheses.claim_boundary: Supports knowledge-constrained planning in one symbolic fire-hydrant scenario; does not establish general GIS competence, final portrayal, ProductLayer resolution, or production authority.
hypotheses.hypothesis_text: A knowledge-grounded mapping agent can generate executable GIS plans that preserve explicit geographic and cartographic constraints more reliably than an unconstrained LLM planner.
hypotheses.independent_variable: Explicit knowledge-derived constraints supplied before planning versus no retrieval evidence or constraints.
negative_evidence: baseline proposal was syntactically valid but blocked before mutation by the common authority gate
fabricated ProductLayer, omitted constraint, unknown tool, contradiction, and postcondition cases fail safely
three failed pre-acceptance attempts are retained
positive_evidence: 7 resolved, 4 bounded unresolved, and 0 contradicted constraints
constrained proposal preserved 6 of 6 applicable constraints and passed 12 of 12 postconditions
knowledge-constrained proposal validated and executed without changing authoritative source data
hypotheses.residual_finding: The paired experiment has one accepted scenario and conservative global constraint-to-step references.
hypotheses.validator: Deterministic proposal schema, semantic precondition gate, allowlist, executor, and postcondition verifier.

hypotheses.claim_boundary: Demonstrates observable planning-layer influence, not optimal planning, minimal explanations, or general interpretability of arbitrary LLM reasoning.
hypotheses.hypothesis_text: Knowledge grounding contributes observably at the planning layer before execution, not merely in the final rendered result.
hypotheses.independent_variable: Presence of the frozen knowledge-derived constraint set during first-pass planning.
negative_evidence: trace references are complete but conservatively global rather than minimal
only one paired accepted run is available
positive_evidence: plans differ before execution in classification, geometry, portrayal, authority, unresolved-state semantics, decision, and trace
all 11 constraint references are represented in the evidence-to-plan trace
hypotheses.residual_finding: Trace completeness is not a measure of explanation quality.
hypotheses.validator: Deterministic comparison of persisted pre-execution drafts and trace references.

hypotheses.claim_boundary: Supports a bounded technical trust and audit boundary for one symbolic proposal; not general AI safety, cybersecurity, institutional authorization, legal acceptability, or production non-repudiation.
controls: zero model calls at trust controls
hypotheses.hypothesis_text: A probabilistic AI-generated mapping proposal can participate in an auditable authoritative workflow when execution is explicitly authorized, proposal-bound, deterministic, independently verified, and provenance-recorded.
hypotheses.independent_variable: Presence or tampering of authorization, proposal identity, scope, tools, parameters, postconditions, provenance, mutation boundary, artifacts, and replay state across Cases A-L.
negative_evidence: Cases B-K reject missing authorization and tampering of proposal, scope, tool, parameters, postconditions, provenance, mutation, unresolved constraints, and artifacts
broad regression retains inherited historical failures rather than hiding them
positive_evidence: canonical positive path accepted with exact proposal ID/hash
authorization, execution, verification, receipt, provenance, and audit records validate
all 12 A-L cases matched expected outcomes and exact replay remained stable
hypotheses.residual_finding: Research identity/time, one proposal, and a bounded adversarial set do not constitute PKI, revocation, trusted time, or exhaustive threat coverage.
hypotheses.validator: Deterministic proposal/authorization hashing, closed-request gate, executor, postcondition verifier, provenance resolver, schema validation, and Boolean final acceptance; zero model calls.
